front: J'ai le cafard depuis qu'il est parti.
pronunciation: [zhay luh kah-FAR duh-pwee keel eh par-TEE]
back: I've been feeling down since he left.
context: 'Avoir le cafard' (to have the cockroach) = to feel low, blue.

front: Il me casse les pieds avec ses histoires.
pronunciation: [eel muh kas lay PYAY ah-vek say zees-TWAHR]
back: He's getting on my nerves with his stories.
context: 'Casser les pieds à quelqu'un' = to annoy someone. 'Casse-pieds' = a pain in the neck.

front: Elle est tombée dans les pommes à cause de la chaleur.
pronunciation: [el eh tohm-bay dahn lay PUM ah kohz duh lah shah-LUHR]
back: She fainted because of the heat.
context: 'Tomber dans les pommes' (fall into the apples) = to faint.

front: Il a un poil dans la main.
pronunciation: [ee lah an pwahl dahn lah MAN]
back: He's bone idle.
context: 'Avoir un poil dans la main' (a hair growing in your palm, from never working) = to be lazy.

front: Arrête de couper les cheveux en quatre !
pronunciation: [ah-ret duh koo-pay lay shuh-vuh ahn KAT-ruh]
back: Stop splitting hairs!
context: 'Couper les cheveux en quatre' = to split hairs.

front: Ce ne sont pas tes oignons.
pronunciation: [suh nuh sohn pah tay zoh-NYOHN]
back: It's none of your business.
context: 'Ce ne sont pas tes oignons' (not your onions) = mind your own business. Informal.

front: Les carottes sont cuites.
pronunciation: [lay kah-rot sohn KWEET]
back: It's all over, nothing more can be done.
context: 'Les carottes sont cuites' (the carrots are cooked) = the situation is hopeless.

front: Arrête de me raconter des salades.
pronunciation: [ah-ret duh muh rah-kohn-tay day sah-LAD]
back: Stop telling me fibs.
context: 'Raconter des salades' = to tell lies, tall stories.

front: Ce matin, j'ai la pêche !
pronunciation: [suh mah-TAN, zhay lah PESH]
back: This morning I'm full of energy!
context: 'Avoir la pêche' (to have the peach) = to feel great. Also 'avoir la frite'.

front: J'ai fait le poireau pendant une heure devant le cinéma.
pronunciation: [zhay feh luh pwah-ROH pahn-dahn tün UHR duh-vahn luh see-nay-MAH]
back: I hung around waiting for an hour outside the cinema.
context: 'Faire le poireau' / 'poireauter' (to be a leek) = to wait for ages.

front: Appuie sur le champignon, on va être en retard !
pronunciation: [ah-pwee sür luh shahn-pee-NYOHN, ohn vah eh-trahn ruh-TAR]
back: Step on it, we're going to be late!
context: 'Appuyer sur le champignon' (press the mushroom) = to put your foot down.

front: Il faut toujours qu'il mette son grain de sel.
pronunciation: [eel foh too-zhoor keel met sohn gran duh SEL]
back: He always has to put his two cents in.
context: 'Mettre son grain de sel' = to butt in with an opinion. Note the subjunctive after 'il faut que'.

front: Excusez-moi, j'ai un chat dans la gorge.
pronunciation: [ek-skü-zay-MWAH, zhay an SHAH dahn lah GORZH]
back: Excuse me, I have a frog in my throat.
context: French has a cat where English has a frog!

front: Je donne ma langue au chat : c'est quoi la réponse ?
pronunciation: [zhuh dun mah lahng oh SHAH : seh KWAH lah ray-POHNS]
back: I give up: what's the answer?
context: 'Donner sa langue au chat' = to give up guessing.

front: Il n'y avait pas un chat dans les rues.
pronunciation: [eel nyah-veh pah zan SHAH dahn lay RÜ]
back: There wasn't a soul in the streets.
context: 'Il n'y a pas un chat' = there's nobody around.

front: J'ai d'autres chats à fouetter.
pronunciation: [zhay doh-truh SHAH ah fweh-TAY]
back: I have bigger fish to fry.
context: Literally 'other cats to whip'.

front: J'ai une faim de loup.
pronunciation: [zhay ün fan duh LOO]
back: I'm ravenous.
context: 'Une faim de loup' (a wolf's hunger) = very hungry.

front: Il est têtu comme une mule.
pronunciation: [ee leh teh-tü kum ün MÜL]
back: He's as stubborn as a mule.
context: Same image as in English.

front: Elle a pris la mouche pour un rien.
pronunciation: [el ah pree lah MOOSH poor an RYAN]
back: She took offense at the slightest thing.
context: 'Prendre la mouche' (to take the fly) = to get touchy.

front: Ça m'a mis la puce à l'oreille.
pronunciation: [sah mah mee lah püs ah loh-RAY]
back: That made me suspicious.
context: 'Mettre la puce à l'oreille' (put the flea in the ear) = to arouse suspicion.

front: Revenons à nos moutons.
pronunciation: [ruh-vuh-nohn ah noh moo-TOHN]
back: Let's get back to the point.
context: 'Revenir à ses moutons' (back to our sheep) = to return to the subject. From a 15th-century farce.

front: Il a promis de rembourser ? Mon œil !
pronunciation: [ee lah proh-mee duh rahm-boor-SAY ? mohn NUHY]
back: He promised to pay back? My foot!
context: 'Mon œil !' (my eye) = I don't believe it, often with a finger pulling down the eyelid.

front: Il a eu les yeux plus gros que le ventre.
pronunciation: [ee lah ü lay zyuh plü groh kuh luh VAHN-truh]
back: His eyes were bigger than his stomach.
context: Same idiom as in English, but with 'ventre' (belly).

front: Si tu crois qu'il va changer, tu te mets le doigt dans l'œil.
pronunciation: [see tü krwah keel vah shahn-ZHAY, tü tuh meh luh dwah dahn LUHY]
back: If you think he'll change, you're kidding yourself.
context: 'Se mettre le doigt dans l'œil' (put your finger in your eye) = to be badly mistaken.

front: Son père a le bras long.
pronunciation: [sohn pehr ah luh brah LOHN]
back: His father has a lot of influence.
context: 'Avoir le bras long' (have a long arm) = to be well connected.

front: Ma voisine m'a tenu la jambe pendant une heure.
pronunciation: [mah vwah-zeen mah tuh-nü lah ZHAHMB pahn-dahn tün UHR]
back: My neighbor kept me talking for an hour.
context: 'Tenir la jambe à quelqu'un' = to keep someone talking (against their will).

front: Arrête de me casser les oreilles avec ta musique !
pronunciation: [ah-ret duh muh kas lay zoh-RAY ah-vek tah mü-ZEEK]
back: Stop deafening me with your music!
context: 'Casser les oreilles' = to be too loud.

front: Elle a la langue bien pendue.
pronunciation: [el ah lah lahng byan pahn-DÜ]
back: She's a real chatterbox.
context: 'Avoir la langue bien pendue' (a well-hung tongue) = to talk a lot, be quick-witted.

front: Il a le cœur sur la main.
pronunciation: [ee lah luh kuhr sür lah MAN]
back: He's very generous.
context: 'Avoir le cœur sur la main' = to be generous and kind.

front: Pardon, j'étais dans la lune.
pronunciation: [par-DOHN, zhay-teh dahn lah LÜN]
back: Sorry, I was miles away.
context: 'Être dans la lune' = to daydream.

front: Quand j'ai appris la nouvelle, je suis tombé des nues.
pronunciation: [kahn zhay ah-pree lah noo-VEL, zhuh swee tohm-bay day NÜ]
back: When I heard the news, I was flabbergasted.
context: 'Tomber des nues' (fall from the clouds) = to be astonished.

front: Si on perd ce client, c'est la fin des haricots.
pronunciation: [see ohn pehr suh klee-YAHN, seh lah fan day zah-ree-KOH]
back: If we lose this client, that's the end of everything.
context: 'La fin des haricots' = the last straw, total disaster (humorous).

front: Il en fait tout un fromage.
pronunciation: [eel ahn feh too tan froh-MAHZH]
back: He's making a big fuss about it.
context: 'En faire tout un fromage' (make a whole cheese of it) = to make a mountain out of a molehill.

front: Il va falloir mettre de l'eau dans ton vin.
pronunciation: [eel vah fah-lwahr meh-truh duh LOH dahn tohn VAN]
back: You'll have to tone it down a bit.
context: 'Mettre de l'eau dans son vin' = to compromise, moderate your demands.

front: Elle est née avec une cuillère d'argent dans la bouche.
pronunciation: [el eh nay ah-vek ün kwee-yehr dar-ZHAHN dahn lah BOOSH]
back: She was born with a silver spoon in her mouth.
context: Same idiom as in English.

front: Tu veux le beurre et l'argent du beurre !
pronunciation: [tü vuh luh BUHR ay lar-zhahn dü BUHR]
back: You want to have your cake and eat it!
context: Literally 'the butter and the money for the butter'.

front: J'ai du pain sur la planche cette semaine.
pronunciation: [zhay dü pan sür lah PLAHNSH set suh-MEN]
back: I have a lot on my plate this week.
context: 'Avoir du pain sur la planche' (bread on the board) = to have a lot of work.

front: Demande-lui, ça ne mange pas de pain.
pronunciation: [duh-mahnd-LWEE, sah nuh mahnzh pah duh PAN]
back: Ask him, it doesn't cost anything.
context: 'Ça ne mange pas de pain' = there's no harm in it.

front: Il a fallu lui tirer les vers du nez.
pronunciation: [ee lah fah-lü lwee tee-ray lay vehr dü NAY]
back: We had to drag it out of him.
context: 'Tirer les vers du nez à quelqu'un' (pull worms from the nose) = to worm information out of someone.

front: Après trois échecs, il a jeté l'éponge.
pronunciation: [ah-preh trwah zay-SHEK, ee lah zhuh-tay lay-POHNZH]
back: After three failures, he threw in the towel.
context: 'Jeter l'éponge' = to give up (from boxing: a sponge, not a towel).

front: Je suis au bout du rouleau.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zoh boo dü roo-LOH]
back: I'm at the end of my tether.
context: 'Être au bout du rouleau' = exhausted, at breaking point.

front: Tu tombes à pic, j'avais besoin d'aide !
pronunciation: [tü tohmb ah PEEK, zhah-veh buh-zwan DED]
back: You've come at just the right time, I needed help!
context: 'Tomber à pic' = to come at the perfect moment.

front: Il a mis les pieds dans le plat pendant le dîner.
pronunciation: [ee lah mee lay pyay dahn luh PLAH pahn-dahn luh dee-NAY]
back: He put his foot in it during dinner.
context: 'Mettre les pieds dans le plat' = to raise an awkward subject tactlessly.

front: Ça ne casse pas trois pattes à un canard.
pronunciation: [sah nuh kas pah trwah PAT ah an kah-NAR]
back: It's nothing to write home about.
context: Literally 'it doesn't break three legs off a duck' (which only has two!). Means: unremarkable.

front: Il ne faut pas vendre la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tué.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh pah vahn-druh lah poh duh LOORS ah-vahn duh lah-vwahr twee-AY]
back: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
context: Literally 'don't sell the bear's skin before you've killed it'.
